{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The present system of financing political campaigns with private contributions is fundamentally anti-democratic.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The present system of financing political campaigns operates as a system of one-dollar/one-vote instead of one-person/one-vote.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Even with the netroots sparking wider interest in campaign funding, the bulk of contributions still come from less than 1 percent of the population.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A system of legalized bribery exists where big contributors buy privileged access to public officials.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Politicians favorable to wealth and privilege benefit, tilting the legislative playing field toward concentrated wealth on every issue.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Public financing of campaigns should be enacted nationally.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Public financing of campaigns has been adopted by several states under the slogan “Clean Money, Clean Elections”.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Senator Paul Wellstone of Minnesota proposed public financing of campaigns.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
